html:
A Japanese electronics and entertainment company founded in Tokyo in 1946 by Masaru Ibuka and Akio Morita, as Tokyo Tsushin Kogyo. It became the symbol of Japan's postwar rise as a maker of quality goods.

The founders started in a bombed out department store, repairing radios. In the 1950s they licensed the transistor from Bell Labs in the United States and put it into small pocket radios, sold around the world from 1957. They chose the short name Sony in 1958 so it would be easy to say in any language. Morita lived in New York for a time to sell the brand in America.

Hits followed:

  • The Trinitron colour television, from 1968.
  • The Walkman portable cassette player, from 1979, which changed how people listened to music.
  • The compact disc, developed with Philips in 1982, and the PlayStation games console in 1994.

Sony also bought Columbia Pictures in 1989 and CBS Records. With Nintendo and Toyota, it carried the made in Japan label from cheap to excellent.
